capabilities.title: Appearance, locale, and date/time/time-zone
capabilities.contract: General Settings persists a System, Light, or Dark appearance preference; the shared resolver maps System to the current device appearance for visual application. It also supports the Interface locale, device-local or explicit IANA time zones, device-local date and time formatting, and explicit date and time formats. Revision History honors saved formatting while generated supporting UI text uses the Interface locale independently of Article language.

capabilities.title: Assistant edit default and request time limit
capabilities.contract: AI assistant Settings shows the default edit mode and request time limit together. The time limit defaults to two minutes and accepts 1, 2, 3, 5, 10, 15, or 30 minutes, or no limit, applying to each new request or retry. The default edit mode proposes edits for review; direct application of explicitly requested edits is opt-in for new Article conversations and never changes an existing conversation. Other Proposals still require review.

capabilities.title: Optional packaged-app telemetry consent
capabilities.contract: During public beta, the packaged Electron app shows a localized, keyboard-accessible default-on switch for a finite pseudonymous diagnostic and usage event contract, plus an enabled-only copyable Telemetry ID for deletion requests. The server emits one finite terminal event after persisted Assistant or direct Editorial completion, or after their failure/cancellation; staged Assistant work is not counted separately. Proposal acceptance captures consent before Revision persistence and emits only after that persistence succeeds. The workspace batches only actual Draft save/discard persistence attempts that began with telemetry enabled into a 30-second in-memory aggregate; no-op checkpoints are excluded. Electron emits one terminal event for each manual, deletion-protective, restore-recovery, or update-recovery SQLite snapshot, plus finite startup, renderer, and child-process failures when the main process remains alive. Main validates each IPC request and event, includes only trusted platform, architecture, and OS-version fields, keeps identity and consent outside Article data, clears both and all in-memory work on opt-out, and treats missing delivery configuration as disabled. Delivery uses an in-memory cap of 100 events per minute and 100 retained events, expires events after five minutes, retries transient failures once without following redirects, and never blocks editorial work. Browser and development runtimes cannot send telemetry.
capabilities.persistence: Electron userData/runtime-settings.json only; it is excluded from SQLite Article data, backups, and restore staging.
limitations: A manually inspected opted-in packaged-beta deletion request, payload, dashboard definitions, and packaged Windows acceptance remain release prerequisites.

capabilities.title: Configurable application shortcuts
capabilities.contract: Settings can persist command overrides and expose conflict-aware shortcut configuration. The Editorial Assistant also supports choosing Enter or Ctrl+Enter as the send key independently of command overrides.
limitations: Complete workspace-action wiring remains tracked separately.

capabilities.title: AI connections and activation
capabilities.contract: Authors choose OpenAI, OpenCode Zen, Anthropic, Google Gemini API, xAI Grok, or DeepSeek before adding an environment-variable connection. In Electron, they first choose an environment variable or managed API key, which Warplyn verifies then stores in Windows Credential Manager or Linux Secret Service. If Secret Service is unavailable or locked, managed credentials report unavailable without a plaintext fallback; environment-variable connections remain usable. Connections are active by default; authors can activate or deactivate each one independently, rename them, test them, or confirm deletion without exposing secret values.

capabilities.title: Default, app, per-skill, reasoning, and favorite-model preferences
capabilities.contract: Imported managed connections without a Warplyn key report actionable Add connection guidance; deleting them leaves the legacy namespace untouched. Each selected model records its active connection as well as its provider model ID, so duplicate model names remain routable and an OpenCode Zen model can disclose its underlying vendor. Default, app, per-skill, reasoning, and favorite-model preferences apply globally. The optional app model is a separate model preference for Warplyn features such as Proposal summaries, titles, and action-intent checks; it falls back to the default model. Authors can save favorite available models, search the available list, and filter it by recognized vendor. Low, medium, and high reasoning-level controls are offered only for selected OpenAI models. Presentation receives Settings through the application service, persistence uses focused repositories, and legacy preferences migrate to their formerly active connection without exposing unknown keys.
capabilities.persistence: Editorial preferences persist in app_settings.application-model-preferences; the independent app model persists in app_settings.application-app-model.

capabilities.title: Available model list refresh
capabilities.contract: Opening AI Settings loads the current model lists for every active OpenAI, OpenCode Zen, Anthropic, Google Gemini API, xAI Grok, or DeepSeek connection; authors can refresh them again to retry or retrieve provider changes. Each returned model retains the connection that supplied it. The OpenAI catalog admits only the gpt-5.5 and gpt-5.6 model families; Zen retains its complete returned catalog. A refreshed list is not proof that every Editorial Operation is supported.
capabilities.persistence: Server-side provider refresh only; the resulting list is not persisted.

capabilities.title: Publishing profiles and language defaults
capabilities.contract: Default, No restrictions, LinkedIn Post, LinkedIn Article, and named custom non-negative limits provide guidance; the selected default applies to new Articles while Articles retain independent selection. Custom profiles have stable IDs, appear before add controls, and require confirmed removal; removing the selected default resets to Default. Settings persists one default Article language and deduplicated translation languages excluding it. Translate creates reviewable proposals for every configured target.

capabilities.title: Browser-selected backup folder, schedule, and retention
capabilities.contract: In supported web browsers, authors explicitly choose a local backup folder. The browser writes complete manifest-bearing backup directories containing a consistent SQLite snapshot, current Author Skills, and immutable Skill Revision history, lists compatible bundles and legacy SQLite snapshots for explicit restore, and reloads after the loopback service safely replaces active data. Daily startup writes at most one automatic backup when the previously selected folder remains permitted, and retention removes only older automatic backups.
capabilities.persistence: app_settings.application-backup-policy plus the browser's local folder permission handle; backup bundles exclude environment variables and API keys.
limitations: Browser bundle transfer supports files up to 100 MB and 500 MB total; larger backups require Electron.

capabilities.title: Explicit Electron local-data deletion
capabilities.contract: In Electron, an author can request deletion of the active resolved Warplyn data directory through a no-argument native operation. The native confirmation explains the irreversible scope and always shows a Create a backup before deletion checkbox, checked only when a separate backup directory is configured. A requested backup must succeed before deletion continues and includes Author Skills with their immutable Skill Revision history. It cancels without changes, closes SQLite and background work before deletion, then exits only after successful removal. The renderer cannot supply a filesystem path.
capabilities.persistence: The confirmed active local data directory is removed. Installer and uninstaller behavior remains data-preserving.

capabilities.title: Explicit local-backup restoration
capabilities.contract: An author chooses a backup from the configured folder and explicitly confirms replacement. Browser restore uploads the selected manifest-bearing bundle through bounded local transfer sessions; the loopback service verifies file hashes and SQLite compatibility before replacing the database and exact saved Skill set, then reopens the application before browser reload. An interrupted browser switch rolls back from a startup recovery marker. Electron uses a staged native restart and verifies its Skill companion manifest before activation. Legacy Skladno backup names and manifest format 1 remain accepted. Validation opens a private copy to avoid writing SQLite sidecars beside the source. Older database-only snapshots leave existing Skills unchanged. The renderer cannot provide an active-data path. Warplyn retains a recovery copy of the database and Skill files and rolls back when restored data cannot open.
capabilities.persistence: A bundle replaces the active SQLite database, Author Skills and Skill Revision history. A legacy database-only snapshot replaces only SQLite. Native and browser restore clear AI connection metadata, environment-variable references, model preferences, and the app model on the private restored database. Other Settings are restored. Source backups and OS credentials remain unchanged. A private recovery copy of the previous database and Skill files, including previous AI settings, remains available for rollback.

capabilities.title: Author-controlled desktop release checks
capabilities.contract: About Settings asks the author in a confirmation dialog to allow GitHub update network access before any discovery request. After consent, it exposes automatic checks and a stable-only or prerelease-inclusive channel preference. Windows exposes explicit download, guarded restart, release notes, and recovery guidance; Linux exposes the newest matching Debian release and its release notes, but no in-app download or apply action. An available release appears in the Article Library utility area and opens About Settings with Updates focused. Browser builds omit the group; Electron development builds expose the persisted preferences but no discovery or download actions.
capabilities.persistence: The desktop runtime file stores the network-permission, automatic-check, and prerelease-channel preferences plus non-content update recovery metadata.

capabilities.title: Repository and license
capabilities.contract: About Settings provides compact external links to the user documentation, GitHub source repository, issue tracker, and MIT License. It keeps these details read-only and opens links in the system browser.
capabilities.persistence: Static application metadata; no author data is stored.

scenarios.title: A saved Assistant edit default applies to new conversations
preconditions: An Author opens AI assistant Settings.
scenarios.event: The Author chooses a default Assistant edit mode.
expected: The choices distinguish reviewable Proposals from directly applied, explicitly requested edits.
The saved value initializes a new Article conversation; existing conversations keep their mode.
forbidden: Changing the mode of an existing conversation without its own control.

scenarios.title: Assistant request time limit is configurable
preconditions: The Author opens AI assistant Settings.
scenarios.event: The Author changes the Assistant request time limit.
expected: The default is two minutes. A labeled control with persistent guidance saves the selected whole-minute limit.
forbidden: An invalid limit disables the deadline.

scenarios.title: General time-zone preferences persist with accessible guidance
scenarios.event: The author selects an explicit IANA time zone or restores the system setting.
expected: The preference is saved with an accessible label, hint, and timestamp preview.
forbidden: Changing display preferences rewrites saved timestamps or Revision history.

scenarios.title: Telemetry remains installation-local and controllable
preconditions: The author opens General Settings in the Electron app.
scenarios.event: The author copies the Telemetry ID, then enables or disables diagnostic and usage data sharing.
expected: A fresh supported beta installation enables telemetry with a new installation ID; a saved opt-out remains disabled.
The main process confirms the persisted value before the switch changes.
The enabled-only Telemetry ID can be copied for a deletion request before opt-out clears it.
Each explicit Assistant or direct Editorial operation sends at most one finite terminal event, with no Article content.
Draft save/discard persistence attempts that started with telemetry enabled are emitted only as a bounded aggregate, with no Article content.
Electron snapshot creation emits one completed or failed finite backup event with no path or snapshot data.
Native backup and Article revision restoration emit one completed or failed recovery event only after their terminal outcome, with no Article content.
Opt-out clears the installation identity and future queued events.
forbidden: Copying consent or the Telemetry ID through Article backup or restore.

scenarios.title: Theme preference applies to the application shell
preconditions: The author has saved a System, Light, or Dark appearance preference.
scenarios.event: The application shell loads the preference or the device appearance changes while System is selected.
expected: Semantic UI tokens apply the selected appearance, and System follows the current device preference.
forbidden: Changing appearance modifies Article content or saved timestamps.

scenarios.title: Key-binding overrides remain conflict-aware
preconditions: The author configures an application shortcut.
scenarios.event: A key binding is normalized and checked against effective commands.
expected: The override can be persisted and conflicts are identified.
forbidden: An override silently replaces a conflicting command.

scenarios.title: AI connection metadata is managed without secrets
preconditions: The author is in the AI Settings section.
scenarios.event: The author adds, activates, deactivates, or confirms removal of a connection.
expected: Authors choose one of the six supported providers and an environment-variable or, in Electron, managed-credential method. Connections are active by default, may share an environment-variable name, and an API key can be verified and stored without being displayed or persisted in Warplyn data.
forbidden: Displaying or persisting API key values.

scenarios.title: Model preferences resolve for editorial and supporting work
preconditions: A default model, app model, skill override, or reasoning effort is saved.
scenarios.event: A new editorial request is prepared.
expected: Editorial work resolves the built-in-skill override or default model through its saved active connection, while Warplyn features resolve the separate app model or default-model fallback. Each selected OpenAI model receives its saved reasoning effort.
forbidden: Exposing unknown legacy override keys.

scenarios.title: Available models load automatically without becoming settings data
preconditions: At least one active AI connection is configured.
scenarios.event: The author opens AI Settings, changes an activation state, or manually refreshes the list.
expected: Every active connection's current model list is offered for selection with its supplying connection, without persisting the refreshed list as preference data.
forbidden: Persisting the refreshed list as a model preference.

scenarios.title: Publishing defaults survive reload
preconditions: The author selects a supported profile and may configure a custom name and non-negative limit.
scenarios.event: The service saves and reloads the profile default.
expected: The selected publishing profile, custom configuration, and language defaults are returned for new Articles and translation requests.
forbidden: Accepting an unknown profile.

scenarios.title: Backups are recoverable without interrupting editing
preconditions: The author opens Data & backups Settings.
scenarios.event: The author chooses a backup folder, creates a manual backup, or the daily schedule runs at application startup.
expected: A complete database and Author Skill bundle is written through the browser permission handle and automatic retention leaves manual backups untouched.
forbidden: A backup failure interrupts Article editing or exposes environment-variable secrets.

scenarios.title: Update controls require author action
preconditions: A packaged desktop release exposes an available release.
scenarios.event: The author opens About Settings, allows update network access, and checks for updates.
expected: The network-permission, automatic-check, and prerelease-channel switches are accessible, a confirmation dialog precedes the persisted network permission, no discovery request occurs before consent, Windows Download appears only after explicit discovery, Linux offers release notes without Download, and the status shows while a Windows update downloads.
forbidden: A browser or development build exposes update controls, an update-discovery request occurs without consent, or a download starts automatically.

scenarios.title: Explicit local-data deletion is contained and backup-gated
preconditions: The author uses the Electron Data & backups Settings section with a resolved local data directory.
scenarios.event: The author cancels deletion, deletes after a native confirmation, or selects backup and deletion.
expected: Cancellation leaves the data unchanged.
A requested backup must complete and be non-empty before deletion proceeds, including Author Skills and their immutable Skill Revision history.
Only the active resolved Warplyn data directory is deleted after background work and SQLite close, and Warplyn exits after success.
forbidden: Deleting an unresolved or broad path.
Continuing to deletion after backup failure.
Deleting local author data during ordinary uninstall.

scenarios.title: Backup restoration is staged and recoverable
preconditions: The author has configured a backup folder containing a Warplyn bundle or legacy SQLite snapshot.
scenarios.event: The author selects a backup and confirms restoration.
expected: Cancellation leaves active data unchanged.

Warplyn validates the selected snapshot, retains a recovery snapshot, and opens the restored Articles, Revisions, Draft checkpoints, Assistant history, style data, Settings, and any backed-up Author Skills with immutable Skill Revision history after restart or browser reload.
Native and browser restore clear saved AI connections and connection-bound model selections; the Author adds connections and selects models again.
Source backups and OS credentials remain unchanged.
If restored startup fails, Warplyn rolls back to the recovery snapshot once, preserving the previous connections and model selections.
forbidden: The renderer supplies an active-data path.
An invalid or incompatible snapshot replaces active data.
Warplyn claims success after a failed replacement or rollback.

scenarios.title: Browser backups recover Author Skills and history
preconditions: The Author has selected a browser backup folder.
scenarios.event: The Author creates and restores a directory backup containing a current Skill and a deleted Skill's history.
expected: The browser transfers the database, current Skill files, and Skill history together, with the manifest written last and checked before restore.
forbidden: A modified or incomplete bundle replaces active data.
A failed backup appears as complete.
